notes: The six packs of 2026-10-28 (Rookery's air constructors, the Damwrights' Beavers, Arc's Welders, Old Mother Brandt's Mammoth, Gladius's Gladiators, Triton's hovers), woven into the roster. Merged by tools/author_bonds_v1.py.

motifs: two who build in the air

C.title: Holding pattern
beats: Noctua's fighters and Atterby's Falcons share a sky for the first time. Nobody collides, which surprises both of them.
You fly them like they're coming home.
They are. I build the home first, then I teach them where it is.
I dream the routes. You pour the runway at the end of them. That's a good night's work.

C.title: Panels on the ridge
beats: Atterby drops solar collectors on a ridge nobody can reach. Solarium is already working out the yield.
South-facing, no shade, nobody to steal the cables. You picked that for the light.
I picked it because it's hard to get to. The light was a bonus.
Then we want the same ground for different reasons. That's the best kind of partnership.

C.title: Foundations
beats: Tarquin paces out a fort on the flat. Atterby is building one on the crag above it.
I don't have to. The cliff is the wall.
Then they'll meet mine first. Yours will hear about it later.

motifs: nests and the weather that comes from above

C.title: Weather report
beats: Thresh's Hailstorm passes over Atterby's shelf base on the way out. The Falcons scramble before anyone has said a word.
Easy. I'm on your side this week.
My birds don't read the contract. They read the bomb bay.
Then keep them on a short leash. Weather doesn't apologise.

motifs: fords are doors, and somebody has to build the frame

C.title: The far bank
beats: Odessa holds a ford. On the far bank, four Beavers are already laying a metal extractor.
I take the crossing, you take the bank?
We take the bank, the bed, and the next bank. You keep the door shut while we pour.
Deal. Don't build a lock on my door.

C.title: Planning permission
beats: Weiss arrives with a survey of the river. Brisk is standing in it.
I need to log where you're building.
Under the water, mostly. You're welcome to come and measure.
There is a form for submerged works.
Then it'll be the first form that gets wet.

motifs: the riverbed and the cliff shelf

C.title: Top and bottom
beats: The company's two newest builders compare notes over a map with water at the bottom and cliffs at the top.
You take everything below the waterline.
You take everything above the treeline.
The middle is where everyone else fights. We just hand them the ground.

C.title: Sit
beats: Varn is pacing the line, hungry for the push. Brandt has not moved the Mammoth all hour.
Sit down, dear. They're coming to us. They always do.
Then you'll have had a nice rest, and you can go hungry later.

C.title: Supper
beats: Bro parks next to the Mammoth and says nothing for a while. Brandt seems to like that.
It's the only spot. Have you eaten?

C.title: Forward
beats: The Kiln walks past the Mammoth toward the turrets. Brandt does not follow.
Forward is where the turrets are, Brakhov. They'll still be there tomorrow.
That's what you said last time, and I had to come and fetch you.

C.title: Manners
beats: Stride's Gunslingers tear past the Mammoth's feet, kicking ash over its armour.
Young man. Slow down and say good evening.
I'll remember that, and so will the Mammoth.

C.title: Encore
beats: Ferro's Gladiators salute an enemy line. Kit Sparkler lights the sky behind them on cue.
I always light up when someone bows.
Then we'll do the whole tour. Every field an arena, every arena a finale.

C.title: Top billing
beats: Stride overtakes the Gladiators mid-feint and steals the kill.
That was my target. Bowing's slow.
Bowing's how the crowd knows who won. Nobody saw you, Stride.

C.title: Expenses
beats: The Auditor reviews the ammunition Ferro's troupe spent on flourishes.
Thirty percent of your shots were theatre.
And a hundred percent of the enemy watched it. What's that worth?
Nothing I can enter in a column.
Then your columns are missing the best part.

motifs: two who read the map in numbers

C.title: Readings
beats: Halq calls a grid square. Calder answers with the hour the water turns over it.
Dry for forty minutes after the second bell.
And that's when I'm already there.

motifs: the straight line and the flood

C.title: Sides
beats: Calder's Tritons hold a perfect line along the shore. The Charybdis comes in wide and floods through it.
I don't believe in lines. Or sides.
The Legion does. I'll be here when you need one to retreat behind.

motifs: the water had better be wide

C.title: Shallows
beats: The Scylla walks out of the sea onto Calder's beach.
For you. The channel is wide enough as far as the second sandbar.
Then I'll stop at the second sandbar.
You won't. But I'll be there when you get stuck.

motifs: the works and the line that guards them
both of them standing in the water

C.title: Breakwater
beats: Brisk's Beavers build on the shoal while Calder's Tritons sit in a line in front of them.
You make a good reason to be one.
Hold till the tide turns and the base is up.
I always know when the tide turns.
